critique: The sprite imagery now reads as individual dandelion seeds rather than intact flower heads, which is closer to the intended botanical look. However, both frames still show seeds born across a broad, nearly full-comp band. From t1 to t4 the dominant change is a denser random field, not a clearly wind-driven dispersal plume emerging from one source and traveling wide. The visible long seed stems also make the drift feel mostly upright/static rather than carried laterally by air.

suggestions.why: Collapse the grid emitter's broad horizontal birth area so the seeds originate from a localized source instead of appearing everywhere at once.
Collapse the vertical birth area to make the motion read as dispersal from one source.
Remove the very deep emitter volume, preventing particles from being initially distributed throughout the frame at different depths.
Tighten the directional spread so the particles form a recognizable wind-blown plume before widening downstream.
